headline: Signed a September motor vehicle abatement and two warrants, and accepted prior meeting minutes.
summary: The Principal Assessor reported that a hearing with Massachusetts Electric before the Appellate Tax Board, set for October 21, 2026, has been continued until February 24, 2027. The Principal Assessor also discussed a conference on accessory dwelling units (ADUs). Afterward, members met in executive session to review abatement and exemption applications, which state law limits to certain people.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the open session and executive session meetings unanimously.
Signed the monthly motor vehicle abatement for September.
Signed the warrant for the income and expense penalties.
Signed the warrant for the sewer liens.

plain_text:
TOWN OF SUTTON
BOARD OF ASSESSORS
 4 UXBRIDGE ROAD
SUTTON, MA  01590-1702
  508-865-8722
Meeting Minutes – October 20, 2026
Present: Robert Nunnemacher, Chairman
 Tracey Tardy, Principal Assessor
 Matthew Read, Assessor
Meeting called to order at 5:00 p.m.
1.         The Board voted unanimously to accept the open session meeting minutes and executive session
            meeting minutes of October 13, 2026
2.         Old & New Business
The Principal Assessor discussed a conference on ADU’s (Accessory Dwelling Unit) she attended
The Principal Assessor advised the Board that the ATB (Appellate Tax Board) hearing with Massachusetts
Electric scheduled for October 21, 2026 has been continued until February 24, 2027
3.         Decisions & Actions Taken
The Board signed the Monthly Motor Vehicle Abatement for September
The Board signed the Warrant for the Income & Expense Penalties
The Board signed the Warrant for the Sewer Liens
4. Adjourned Open Session @ 5:30 to enter into Executive Session regarding
            Abatements/Exemptions
The Board entered into executive session to review abatement and/or exemption applications pursuant
to Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 59, Section 60, and Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7. We are 
meeting in executive session to comply with Chapter 59, Section 60, which limits inspection of Chapter 59 
abatement and exemption applications to assessors and the deputies, clerks and assistants of the assessors, and 
certain other parties listed in the law. Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7 permits public bodies to meet in 
executive session for the purpose of complying with general laws. 
The Board of Assessors adjourned its open meeting at or about 5:30 p.m. 
Respectfully Submitted,
Linda Hicks, Assistant Assessor
